implementation.improvement: Added a shared flush helper and a zero-copy direct path for full submit_many() chunks. When the batcher has no pending buffered entries and a chunk exactly fills the configured maximum, the kernel ioctl receives the caller's validated array pointer directly instead of copying the chunk into the internal buffer.
implementation.partial_safety: Partial chunks and all partial completions continue to use the internal retry buffer. If a direct ioctl completes only part of a chunk or fails, uncompleted entries are copied into the buffer and remain retryable.
implementation.bounds: Direct chunks remain limited to the configured 1..64 kernel batch size. submit_many() retains its 4096-entry input bound and validates every entry before submission.
implementation.security: The direct path only changes userspace pointer selection; kernel ioctl authorization, lineage, tenant isolation, overflow checks, telemetry-loss handling, and admission checks remain authoritative.

productivity_interpretation.benefit: A full eight-entry coalesced chunk reaches the batch ioctl through the original caller array, avoiding one userspace copy while retaining direct-path completion accounting. The controlled benchmark also retains the M161 two-to-one ioctl reduction.
productivity_interpretation.scope: This proves pointer-path and submission-count behavior, not end-to-end latency or memory-bandwidth improvement on physical accelerators.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate retained the inherited M155 synthetic QEMU accounting benchmark at speedup_x100=124 in this run; M162 does not claim an isolated raw-throughput gain.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M162 is userspace runtime/test integration.

release_gate.reason: M162 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: Direct pointer use is safe only for the duration of the synchronous ioctl; this API does not support asynchronous retention by the kernel.
The measured copy avoidance is a controlled full-chunk unit path, not a hardware memory-bandwidth benchmark.
The unit test uses an injected ioctl model; QEMU validates integration and packaging, not physical accelerator behavior.
No isolated M162 raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark remains supporting context only.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
